name: ZITLAS Sprouted Moong Sheera Bowl
description: A savoury-sweet sheera made from ground sprouted moong instead of rava — a distinct grain-free take on the traditional semolina sheera already in the database.
instructions: Heat ghee in a kadai, add ground moong sprouts and roast for 3-4 minutes.
Add milk gradually, stirring continuously.
Once thickened, stir in jaggery and cook 2 more minutes.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Moong sprouts base gives notably more protein and fiber than the semolina used in a traditional sheera
Distinct grain-free composition from the Rava Sheera Protein Bowl already in the database
Naturally sweet, comforting texture

name: ZITLAS Nachni Ambil Breakfast Bowl
description: A fermented ragi (nachni) porridge mixed with curd — a ragi-based variant of the bajra Dahi Ambil already in the database, offering a genuinely different grain and mineral profile.
ingredients: Roasted cumin powder, black salt — 2 g
instructions: Whisk ragi flour with water and let it ferment at room temperature for 8-10 hours.
Cook the fermented mixture for 8-10 minutes until slightly thickened, then cool.
Mix in curd, roasted cumin powder and black salt.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.
why_it_works: Ragi's calcium content gives this a genuinely different mineral profile from the bajra-based Dahi Ambil already in the database
Same fermentation technique applied to a different grain
Cooling, probiotic breakfast

name: ZITLAS Nagpur-Style Curd Rice with Orange
description: Curd rice finished with fresh orange segments instead of pomegranate or peanuts — a Nagpur-inspired twist celebrating the city's famous citrus crop.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, oil — 3 ml
instructions: Mash the cold rice slightly and mix with curd.
Quickly temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in a few drops of oil and stir in.
Top with fresh orange segments just before serving.
Serve chilled.
why_it_works: Orange is a genuinely distinct topping from the peanut or pomegranate versions of curd rice already in the database, and specifically nods to Nagpur's famous orange orchards
Almost entirely no-cook
Bright, citrusy contrast to the tempered rice

name: ZITLAS Sabudana Idli-Style Steamed Bites
description: Soaked sabudana steamed in an idli mould instead of shaped into khichdi, vada or thalipeeth — a fourth genuinely distinct format for the same fasting-day ingredient.
instructions: Mix soaked sabudana with curd, crushed peanuts, green chilli and cumin seeds.
Spoon into greased idli moulds.
Steam in a pressure cooker (without the whistle) for 10-12 minutes until set.
Unmould and serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Idli-mould steaming is a genuinely different construction from the khichdi, vada or thalipeeth uses of sabudana already in the database
Curd binds the sabudana without needing potato
Portion-controlled, bite-sized format

name: ZITLAS Moong Amboli
description: Amboli made with ground moong dal instead of urad dal — a protein-boosted, genuinely different legume base from the classic Konkan amboli already in the database.
instructions: Soak rice and moong dal separately, then grind together with a little cooked rice into a thick batter.
Ferment for 6-8 hours.
Heat a tawa, pour a thick ladle of batter and spread only slightly.
Cover and cook until the top sets with small holes, then flip briefly.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Moong dal ferments and cooks differently from urad dal, giving a genuinely different flavour and slightly higher protein than the classic amboli already in the database
Same thick, spongy Konkan technique, different legume
Good protein-forward alternative for users who prefer moong over urad

name: ZITLAS Besan Ghavan
description: A thin rice-and-besan crepe, distinct from the plain rice-flour Ghavan already in the database by its added protein and slightly nutty flavour.
instructions: Whisk rice flour and besan with water into a thin, watery batter; rest 10 minutes.
Heat a tawa, pour a thin layer of batter and spread quickly.
Cook until the edges lift, without needing to flip.
Serve warm with chutney or jaggery.
why_it_works: Besan addition gives more protein than the plain rice-flour ghavan already in the database, while keeping the same thin, unfermented technique
Quick, no fermentation wait
Distinct nutty flavour from the plain version

name: ZITLAS Chana Misal Breakfast Bowl
description: A misal-style curry made from boiled chana instead of sprouted matki — a distinct legume base from the Misal Pav Bowl and Farsan-Free Sprouts Misal Bowl already in the database.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add tomato and cook soft.
Add boiled chana and goda masala with water to form a moderately thick gravy; simmer 8-10 minutes.
Serve hot with a squeeze of lemon.
why_it_works: Chana as the base legume is a genuinely different choice from the matki used in every other misal-style recipe already in the database
Milder, less bitter flavour than matki, appealing to a different palate
Same misal technique, different pulse

name: ZITLAS Bajri Ambil with Peanuts
description: A bajra ambil finished with crushed peanuts instead of just curd — a textured, protein-boosted variant of the plain Dahi Ambil already in the database.
ingredients: Roasted cumin powder, black salt — 2 g
instructions: Whisk bajra flour with water and ferment at room temperature for 8-10 hours.
Cook the fermented mixture for 8-10 minutes until slightly thickened, then cool.
Stir in crushed peanuts, roasted cumin powder and black salt.
Serve at room temperature.
why_it_works: Peanuts add crunch and meaningfully more protein than the curd-only Dahi Ambil already in the database
Fully vegan alternative to the dairy-based version
Same fermentation technique, different finishing

name: ZITLAS Steamed Moong Patodi Breakfast Bites
description: Steamed squares made from ground moong dal instead of besan — a distinct legume base from the besan Patodi already in the database.
ingredients: Moong dal, soaked and ground — 120 g
instructions: Grind soaked moong dal with curd and turmeric into a thick batter.
Pour into a greased tin and steam in a pressure cooker (without the whistle) for 12-15 minutes.
Cool slightly and cut into squares.
Temper sesame seeds in oil and pour over the top.
why_it_works: Moong dal base gives notably more protein than the besan Patodi already in the database
Denser, nuttier texture from the whole-legume base
Same steaming and tempering technique, different pulse

name: ZITLAS Kairi Panha with Sattu Combo
description: A traditional raw mango cooler (panha) paired with a side of sattu for protein — a distinct drink-plus-protein breakfast combination for hot Maharashtra summers.
ingredients: Raw mango, boiled and pulped — 80 g
instructions: Boil the raw mango until soft, then pulp it.
Mix the pulp with jaggery and water to make a tangy-sweet panha; dilute to a drinkable consistency.
Separately whisk sattu with a little water and roasted cumin powder into a thick drink.
Serve both side by side — the panha for cooling, the sattu for protein.
why_it_works: Panha (a diluted raw mango drink) is distinct from the thick Aamras already in the database, which uses ripe mango and isn't diluted
Pairing with sattu specifically addresses panha's very low protein content
Traditional Maharashtrian summer cooler with a genuine fitness purpose added

name: ZITLAS Toor Dal Amti Thali with Solkadhi
description: A complete lunch thali combining toor dal amti, rice, and a small side of solkadhi — a multi-component meal structure distinct from a single dal-and-rice bowl.
instructions: Pressure cook toor dal until soft, then temper with goda masala and a little jaggery to make amti.
Separately mix kokum water with coconut milk for a small side of solkadhi.
Serve the amti over rice with the solkadhi alongside as a palate-cleansing drink.
why_it_works: Thali format with a purposeful solkadhi side is a genuinely different meal structure from a plain amti bowl
Solkadhi traditionally aids digestion after a legume-heavy meal
Complete, considered Maharashtrian lunch structure

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Kolhapuri Rassa Bowl
description: A vegetable-only version of the fiery Kolhapuri rassa gravy — using the same dried-chilli paste as the meat and egg versions, but built around vegetables for a fully plant-based option.
ingredients: Dried Kolhapuri red chillies, ground — 6 g
instructions: Fry sliced onion until golden, blend with dried Kolhapuri chillies, garlic and coconut into a paste.
Heat oil, cook the paste until fragrant.
Add the vegetables and water, and simmer 15-18 minutes until tender.
Serve hot with rice or bhakri.
why_it_works: Gives fully plant-based users access to the same distinctive Kolhapuri flavour used for the meat, egg, soya and paneer versions across the database
Lowest-cost of the Kolhapuri-style dishes
Genuine vegetable-forward option within the regional flavour family

name: ZITLAS Chicken Sukka Lunchbox Wrap
description: Dry-cooked spiced chicken sukka wrapped in a roti specifically for an office lunchbox — a portable format distinct from the bowl-served Kombdi Sukka already in the database.
instructions: Cook the chicken with coconut and Malvani masala, allowing the mixture to dry down completely rather than staying saucy.
Roll out and roast the atta into a roti.
Spread the dry sukka onto the roti and roll tightly.
Wrap in foil — it travels well for several hours.
why_it_works: Wrap format is a genuinely different delivery method from the bowl-served Kombdi Sukka already in the database, engineered specifically for lunchbox portability
Dry preparation means no leaking or sogginess over a few hours
Same regional flavour, different practical purpose

name: ZITLAS Baked Malvani-Style Fish
description: Fish marinated in Malvani spices and baked instead of pan-fried — a distinct cooking technique from the curry or sukka fish preparations already in the database.
instructions: Marinate the fish in Malvani masala and turmeric for 10 minutes.
Coat lightly in rice flour.
Arrange on a lightly oiled tray and bake at 200°C for 12-15 minutes, turning once, until crisp and cooked through.
Serve with lemon wedges.
why_it_works: Baking is a genuinely different technique from the wet curry (Malvani Fish Curry) or dry masala-roast (Prawn/Chicken Sukka) preparations already in the database
Traditionally this dish would be pan-fried in generous oil; baking meaningfully cuts the fat
Crisp texture without deep frying

name: ZITLAS Paneer Bhaji with Bhakri
description: Paneer cooked in a simple onion-tomato Maharashtrian home-style bhaji with goda masala — distinct from the fiery Paneer Kolhapuri Bowl already in the database by its milder, everyday preparation.
instructions: Knead jowar flour into a bhakri and cook on a tawa.
Heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft, add goda masala.
Add paneer cubes and a little water, simmering gently 5-6 minutes.
Serve hot with the bhakri.
why_it_works: Milder, everyday home-style bhaji preparation is genuinely different from the fiery dried-chilli-paste Kolhapuri version already in the database
Bhakri pairing rather than roti or rice
Simple, quick, family-friendly

name: ZITLAS Masoor Khichdi Maharashtra-Style
description: A khichdi made with whole masoor and rice, flavoured with goda masala — a distinct spice profile from the plain or Gujarati-style khichdis already in the database.
instructions: Rinse rice and masoor together.
Heat oil, temper with goda masala, saute vegetables briefly, then add the rice and masoor.
Add water and pressure cook for 3 whistles until soft.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Goda masala gives this khichdi a distinctly Maharashtrian sweet-spicy character, different from the plain or North Indian khichdis already in the database
Whole masoor cooks faster than most other legumes, making this a quicker option
One-pot, minimal cleanup

name: ZITLAS Egg Bhaji with Bhakri
description: A home-style Maharashtrian egg curry with goda masala, milder and simpler than the Kolhapuri or saoji versions already in the database — everyday comfort food.
instructions: Knead jowar flour into a bhakri and cook on a tawa.
Heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft, add goda masala.
Add water to form a gravy, then halve the boiled eggs and simmer 3-4 minutes.
Serve hot with the bhakri.
why_it_works: Everyday goda-masala-based egg preparation is milder and simpler than the Kolhapuri or Vidarbha saoji egg curries already in the database, genuinely representing typical home cooking
Budget-friendly protein option
Bhakri pairing

name: ZITLAS Tondli Bhaji Bowl
description: Ivy gourd (tondli) stir-fried Maharashtrian-style — introducing a vegetable not used anywhere else in the database, a common everyday Maharashtrian sabzi.
instructions: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and turmeric.
Add sliced tondli and saute, covered, for 10-12 minutes until tender, stirring occasionally.
Stir in crushed peanuts for the last 2 minutes.
Serve with rice or bhakri.
why_it_works: Ivy gourd is a genuinely new vegetable for the database, a very common everyday Maharashtrian sabzi rarely represented in fitness recipe collections
Peanuts add crunch and protein a plain sabzi would lack
Simple, quick, budget-friendly

name: ZITLAS Val Dal Khichdi
description: A khichdi made from val (field beans) combined with rice — a distinct legume-khichdi combination from the moong, masoor or bajra khichdis already in the database.
instructions: Heat oil, temper with goda masala.
Add rice and boiled val beans with water, and pressure cook for 2-3 whistles until soft.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Val is a genuinely new legume choice for a khichdi in the database, distinct from moong, masoor or the millet-based versions already used
Winter-season Maharashtrian legume, adding seasonal variety
Simple, one-pot

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Amboli Wrap
description: A ghavan/amboli-style crepe rolled around a vegetable filling — a wrap format for a traditionally flat, plate-served Konkan crepe.
instructions: Whisk rice flour with water into a thin batter and cook a ghavan on a tawa.
Heat a little oil, saute vegetables with green chilli until soft.
Spread the vegetable filling onto the warm ghavan and roll tightly.
Serve immediately.
why_it_works: Rolling the traditionally flat ghavan into a wrap is a genuinely different eating format from serving it plain with chutney or jaggery
Portable for a lunchbox, unlike a plate-served crepe
Vegetable-forward, low calorie

name: ZITLAS Paneer Malvani Bowl
description: Paneer simmered in a coconut-based Malvani gravy — a vegetarian dairy option within the Malvani flavour family, parallel to the Tofu Malvani Bowl already in the database.
instructions: Grind grated coconut with Malvani masala into a paste.
Heat oil, saute onion, add the coconut paste and cook until fragrant.
Add water to form a gravy, then gently add the paneer and simmer 5-6 minutes.
Serve hot with rice.
why_it_works: Gives users a dairy-protein choice within the Malvani flavour family, alongside the already-existing Tofu Malvani Bowl
Paneer's mildness absorbs the coconut-forward masala well
Same coastal regional identity, different protein

name: ZITLAS Fish Kolhapuri Bowl
description: Fish cooked in the deep-red Kolhapuri dried-chilli paste — a distinctly different regional treatment of fish from the coconut-forward Malvani fish curry already in the database.
ingredients: Dried Kolhapuri red chillies, ground — 6 g
instructions: Fry sliced onion until golden, blend with dried Kolhapuri chillies, garlic and coconut into a paste.
Heat oil, cook the paste until fragrant.
Add water to form a gravy, then gently add the fish and simmer 6-8 minutes until just cooked.
Serve hot with rice.
why_it_works: Kolhapuri's inland, deep-fried-onion-based masala is a genuinely different regional treatment of fish from the coastal Malvani coconut-based curry already in the database
Uncommon pairing of Kolhapuri masala with fish (usually used for meat), offering real variety
Deep red, intensely flavoured

name: ZITLAS Chicken Amti-Style Light Dinner
description: Chicken cooked in a tangy, kokum-soured amti-style gravy — a lighter, souring-forward preparation distinct from the richer Kolhapuri rassa or Malvani curries already in the database.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add goda masala.
Add the chicken, kokum and a little jaggery with water; simmer 18-20 minutes until tender.
Serve hot, deliberately lighter and tangier than a coconut-based curry.
why_it_works: Kokum souring rather than coconut milk or dried-chilli paste gives this a genuinely lighter, tangier profile than the richer curries already in the database
Suited to an evening meal that shouldn't feel too heavy
Same amti technique used for legumes in this collection, applied to chicken

name: ZITLAS Soya Sukka Dinner Bowl
description: Dry, roasted spiced soya chunks with coconut — a plant-based parallel to the Kombdi Sukka and Malvani Prawn Sukka already in the database.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until golden.
Add Malvani masala and grated coconut, roasting until fragrant.
Add the soya chunks and a small splash of water, cooking down until dry and roasted rather than saucy, about 8-10 minutes.
Serve as a dry side.
why_it_works: Completes the dry-sukka technique across a fully plant-based protein, alongside the chicken and prawn versions already in the database
High protein, budget-friendly
Distinct texture from any wet-gravy soya preparation elsewhere

name: ZITLAS Egg Kolhapuri Dinner Wrap
description: The Kolhapuri-style egg curry, dried down and wrapped in a roti — a portable dinner-wrap format distinct from the bowl-served Kolhapuri-Style Egg Curry Bowl already in the database.
instructions: Roll out and roast the atta into a roti.
Cook chopped boiled egg in oil with sliced onion and Kolhapuri masala, letting the mixture dry down rather than staying saucy.
Spread onto the roti and roll tightly.
Serve warm, or wrap for later.
why_it_works: Dry, wrap-friendly construction is a genuinely different eating format from the bowl-served Kolhapuri egg curry already in the database
Same fiery regional flavour, different practical delivery
Good for a quick, portable dinner

name: ZITLAS Prawn Kolhapuri Bowl
description: Prawns cooked in the deep-red Kolhapuri dried-chilli paste — distinct from the coconut-based Malvani prawn preparations already in the database by its inland spice base.
ingredients: Dried Kolhapuri red chillies, ground — 6 g
instructions: Fry sliced onion until golden, blend with dried Kolhapuri chillies, garlic and coconut into a paste.
Heat oil, cook the paste until fragrant.
Add water to form a gravy, then add the prawns and simmer just 4-5 minutes until cooked through.
Serve over rice.
why_it_works: Kolhapuri masala applied to prawns is a genuinely different regional pairing from the Malvani (coastal, coconut-forward) prawn dishes already in the database
Prawns cook fast, keeping this quick despite the elaborate paste
Deep, intense inland spice character with a coastal protein

name: ZITLAS Mutton Sukka Dinner Bowl
description: Dry, deeply roasted spiced mutton with coconut — distinct from the wet Kolhapuri Mutton Rassa already in the database by its dry, roasted texture.
instructions: Pressure cook the mutton with a little water until tender, about 15-18 minutes.
Heat oil, saute onion, add Malvani masala and grated coconut, roasting until fragrant.
Add the cooked mutton and cook down on medium heat, stirring, until dry and roasted rather than saucy, about 10-12 minutes.
Serve as a dry side.
why_it_works: Dry sukka texture gives users a genuinely different way to eat mutton from the wet rassa curry already in the database
Pressure cooking first keeps the mutton tender despite the final dry-roasting step
Concentrated, intensely flavoured

name: ZITLAS Tofu Kolhapuri Bowl
description: Tofu simmered in Kolhapuri masala — completes the set of Kolhapuri-style proteins with a fully vegan dairy-free option, distinct from the coconut-based Tofu Malvani Bowl already in the database.
ingredients: Dried Kolhapuri red chillies, ground — 6 g
instructions: Fry sliced onion until golden, blend with dried Kolhapuri chillies, garlic and coconut into a paste.
Heat oil, cook the paste until fragrant.
Add water to form a gravy, then gently add the tofu and simmer 6-8 minutes.
Serve hot with rice.
why_it_works: Uses the inland Kolhapuri masala rather than the coastal Malvani base already applied to tofu in the database, giving genuinely different regional flavour variety for the same protein
Fully vegan, high protein
Completes the six-protein Kolhapuri set (mutton, chicken, egg, soya, paneer, tofu) across the database

name: ZITLAS Post-Workout Chicken Amti Bowl
description: Chicken cooked in a tangy kokum amti gravy over rice, specifically timed and portioned for right after an evening workout — a non-vegetarian counterpart to the Post-Workout Soya Amti Bowl already in the database.
instructions: Heat oil, temper with goda masala.
Add chicken, kokum and a little jaggery with water; simmer 18-20 minutes until tender.
Serve hot over rice within 45-60 minutes of finishing an evening workout.
why_it_works: Gives non-vegetarian users a post-workout-timed option alongside the soya version already in the database, using the same amti technique with more complete-protein content from chicken
Rice provides fast-digesting carbohydrate for glycogen replenishment
Explicit timing purpose distinct from a general-purpose chicken amti

name: ZITLAS Family-Style Kolhapuri Mixed Vegetable Rassa Platter
description: A larger-batch version of the Vegetable Kolhapuri Rassa Bowl, plated with rice for sharing across a family — distinct from the individual lunch portion by scale and serving format.
ingredients: Dried Kolhapuri red chillies, ground — 14 g
instructions: Fry sliced onion until golden, blend with dried Kolhapuri chillies, garlic and coconut into a paste.
Heat oil, cook the paste until fragrant.
Add the vegetables and water, and simmer 18-20 minutes until tender.
Serve family-style on a large platter with rice, for three people to share.
why_it_works: Scaled specifically for family sharing rather than an individual lunch portion, a genuinely different meal-planning purpose from the Vegetable Kolhapuri Rassa Bowl already in the database
Budget-friendly way to feed several people the same distinctive regional flavour
Same recipe, deliberately different serving context

name: ZITLAS Chana Usal Snack Bowl
description: A dry-roasted chana usal, portioned as an evening snack rather than a full meal — distinct from the Chana Misal Breakfast Bowl by its smaller portion and drier consistency.
instructions: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and turmeric, saute onion briefly.
Add boiled chana and toss for 4-5 minutes until warmed through and dry.
Serve as a light evening snack.
why_it_works: Small, dry-tossed portion is genuinely different from the gravy-based breakfast misal preparations already in the database
Quick, minimal ingredients
Good light evening protein snack

name: ZITLAS Moong Sprouts Chaat Snack
description: A quick no-cook moong sprouts chaat sized as an evening snack — light and fast to assemble.
instructions: Toss moong sprouts with onion and tomato.
Add lemon juice and chaat masala.
Eat immediately.
why_it_works: Genuinely quick, no-cook evening snack with real protein and fiber
Light enough not to interfere with dinner
Simple, minimal cleanup

name: ZITLAS Roasted Makhana Kolhapuri Masala Snack
description: Roasted makhana tossed with Kolhapuri spice powder — a fiery Maharashtrian-flavoured spin on makhana, distinct from the plain, chaat-style or trail-mix uses already in the database.
instructions: Dry-roast the makhana in oil until crisp, 4-5 minutes.
Toss with Kolhapuri masala powder while still warm.
Cool slightly and serve.
why_it_works: Kolhapuri spicing is a genuinely different flavour direction from the plain, chaat-style or trail-mix uses of makhana already in the database
Very low calorie, high volume snack
Quick, shelf-stable if made in a batch

name: ZITLAS Baked Kanda Bhajiya Curd Dip Snack
description: Baked onion fritter bites served with a cooling curd dip — a distinct pairing from the plain Baked Kanda Bhaji Bites already in the database, which had no dip.
instructions: Mix sliced onion with besan, red chilli powder and a little water to bind.
Shape into small mounds and bake at 200°C for 15 minutes until golden.
Serve with a bowl of plain curd for dipping.
why_it_works: Curd dip pairing gives this meaningfully more protein than the plain baked bhaji bites already in the database, and a cooling contrast to the spice
Baked, not fried, keeping fat low
Distinct serving format from the earlier version

name: ZITLAS Sprouted Matki Chaat Snack Cup
description: A no-cook sprouted matki chaat in a portable cup — distinct from the cooked Matki-based dishes already in the database by being entirely raw and quick.
instructions: Toss raw sprouted matki with onion and tomato.
Add lemon juice and chaat masala.
Eat immediately for maximum crunch.
why_it_works: Raw, crunchy sprouts give a genuinely different texture from every cooked matki dish already in the database
Entirely no-cook, fast evening snack
Portable cup format

name: ZITLAS Baked Batata Wada-Style Bites
description: Spiced mashed potato balls, baked instead of the traditional deep-fried batata wada — a lighter take on the iconic Mumbai vada pav filling, served as standalone bites.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, turmeric, green chilli — 5 g
instructions: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds, add turmeric and green chilli, then mashed potato, mixing well.
Shape into small balls and roll lightly in besan.
Bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Serve with green chutney.
why_it_works: Baking instead of deep-frying meaningfully cuts the fat of Mumbai's iconic batata wada while keeping the familiar shape and spice
Served as standalone bites rather than inside a pav, distinct from the earlier Soya Stuffed Pav or Dabeli
Popular street food made genuinely lighter

name: ZITLAS Corn Bhel Maharashtrian-Style
description: A bhel made with boiled sweet corn as the base instead of puffed rice or poha — a genuinely different bhel composition from the Puffed Rice Bhel Bowl already in the database.
instructions: Combine boiled corn, onion, tomato and peanuts in a bowl.
Add tamarind chutney and lemon juice.
Toss well and eat immediately.
why_it_works: Corn as the base is a genuinely different composition from the puffed-rice bhel already in the database
Naturally sweet-savoury balance from the corn itself
Entirely no-cook

name: ZITLAS Peanut Masala Sundal Snack
description: Boiled peanuts tempered Maharashtrian-style with mustard seeds and curry leaves — a distinct dry, tempered peanut snack from the boiled or roasted uses of peanuts already in the database.
ingredients: Raw peanuts, boiled and shelled — 80 g
Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric — 3 g
instructions: Boil raw peanuts until soft, then shell them.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds, curry leaves and turmeric, saute onion briefly.
Add the boiled peanuts and toss for 3-4 minutes.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Tempered warm-snack format is a genuinely different way to eat boiled peanuts from the cold chaat-style Boiled Peanut Chaat Bowl already in the database
South Indian sundal technique applied to a Maharashtrian everyday snack
Quick, budget-friendly

name: ZITLAS Roasted Chana Chivda Snack Mix
description: A dry chivda made from roasted chana, peanuts and light spices, without any rice or poha base — a distinct pulse-only chivda from the poha-, puffed-rice- or roti-based chivdas already in the database.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric — 3 g
instructions: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds, curry leaves and turmeric.
Add roasted chana and peanuts, tossing for 3-4 minutes to coat well.
Cool and store, or eat warm.
why_it_works: Pulse-only composition (no rice, poha or roti) is a genuinely different chivda base from every other chivda already in the database
Higher protein per serving than a grain-based chivda
Batch-makeable, keeps for days

name: ZITLAS Curd Sabudana Snack Bowl
description: A small, snack-sized portion of sabudana mixed cold with curd — distinct from the full-meal khichdi, vada or thalipeeth uses of sabudana by its smaller, no-cook format.
ingredients: Roasted cumin powder, black salt — 2 g
instructions: Mix boiled, cooled sabudana into curd.
Season with roasted cumin powder and black salt.
Eat as a light snack, not a full meal.
why_it_works: Small, curd-based, no-cook portion is genuinely different from every other sabudana preparation in the database, all of which are full-meal formats
Very light, cooling
Quick to assemble if sabudana is pre-boiled

name: ZITLAS Sprouts Peanut Farsan-Free Bhel
description: Mixed sprouts and peanuts tossed bhel-style without any fried farsan or puffed rice — a distinct composition from the Puffed Rice Bhel Bowl or Corn Bhel already in this collection.
instructions: Combine mixed sprouts, peanuts, onion and tomato.
Add tamarind chutney and lemon juice.
Toss and eat immediately.
why_it_works: No fried farsan or puffed rice base keeps this notably lower in refined carbohydrate than a standard bhel, and higher in protein from the sprouts
Entirely no-cook
High fiber, filling despite being light

name: ZITLAS Steamed Moong Vada Snack
description: Moong dal vadas steamed rather than fried or air-fried — a genuinely different cooking technique from the Air-Fried Urad Dal Vada or Air-Fried Chana Dal Vada already in the database.
ingredients: Moong dal, soaked and ground — 100 g
instructions: Grind soaked moong dal with ginger and green chilli into a thick batter; mix in onion.
Shape into small discs.
Steam in a pressure cooker (without the whistle) for 12-15 minutes until firm.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Steaming rather than air-frying is a genuinely different technique from the vadas already in the database, using zero added oil in the vada itself
Softer texture than a fried or air-fried vada
High protein, minimal fat

name: ZITLAS Roasted Peanut Thecha Dip Snack Bowl
description: The Maharashtrian peanut-garlic thecha served as a dip with raw vegetable sticks — a distinct serving format from the Thecha Peanut Sandwich already in the database.
instructions: Pound or blend roasted peanuts with garlic and green chilli into a thick, coarse thecha paste.
Cut cucumber and carrot into sticks.
Serve the thecha as a dip alongside the vegetable sticks.
why_it_works: Dip-with-vegetables format is a genuinely different way to eat thecha from the bread-sandwich version already in the database
Very low calorie overall thanks to the raw vegetable base
Quick, no cooking needed

name: ZITLAS Curd Roasted Chana Snack Cup
description: Roasted chana folded into curd as a portable snack cup — a distinct combination and format from the breakfast Roasted Chana Dal and Curd Bowl already in the database.
instructions: Fold roasted chana into curd.
Season with roasted cumin powder.
Eat as a light evening snack, portioned smaller than the breakfast bowl version.
why_it_works: Smaller, snack-portioned version distinct from the full breakfast-bowl serving already in the database
Genuinely zero cooking
Good light evening protein option

name: ZITLAS Roasted Peanut Jaggery Bites Snack
description: A quick no-bake peanut-jaggery bite sized as a small evening snack rather than a meal-replacement bar — distinct portioning from the meal-prep chikki bites already in the database.
instructions: Melt jaggery with ghee in a small pan on low heat until syrupy.
Mix in crushed peanuts, coating evenly.
Shape into 2-3 small bites while still warm.
Cool before eating.
why_it_works: Single-serving snack portion, distinct from the batch-made meal-prep chikki bites already in the database
Quick to make fresh rather than stored for the week
Simple, minimal ingredients

name: ZITLAS Nagpur Orange Peel Chivda
description: A dry chivda mixed with finely grated dried orange peel — a genuinely unique Nagpur specialty celebrating the city's famous orange crop, distinct from any other chivda in the database.
ingredients: Dried orange peel, finely grated — 8 g
Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric — 3 g
instructions: Dry-roast the poha until crisp.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds, curry leaves and turmeric, roast the peanuts.
Toss the roasted poha with the tempering and grated dried orange peel.
Cool and store, or eat warm.
why_it_works: Dried orange peel is a genuinely unique Nagpur ingredient not used anywhere else in the database, giving a distinct citrus-forward chivda
Nagpur is famously known as 'Orange City', and this recipe deliberately celebrates that regional identity
Batch-makeable, keeps for days

name: ZITLAS Bhakarwadi-Inspired Baked Rolls
description: Maharashtra's famous spiral-rolled, spiced snack, baked instead of deep-fried — a distinct rolled-and-sliced construction not resembling any other recipe in the database.
ingredients: Sesame seeds, poppy seeds, coriander seeds — 10 g
instructions: Knead besan and atta with a little oil and water into a firm dough; roll out into a large thin sheet.
Spread a paste of sesame seeds, poppy seeds, coriander seeds, tamarind and jaggery evenly over the sheet.
Roll tightly into a log, then slice into thin rounds.
Arrange the spirals on a tray and bake at 190°C for 18-20 minutes until crisp.
Cool completely before storing.
why_it_works: The spiral roll-and-slice construction is genuinely unlike any other recipe in the database
Baking dramatically cuts the fat of the traditionally deep-fried snack while keeping the signature texture
One of Maharashtra's most iconic tea-time snacks, made into a lighter everyday option

name: ZITLAS Kanda Lasun Masala Curd Bowl
description: A curd bowl seasoned with Kolhapur's famous kanda-lasun (onion-garlic) masala powder instead of the usual cumin — an unusual but genuinely distinct use of a spice blend normally reserved for curries.
instructions: Whisk kanda-lasun masala powder into curd.
Top with crushed roasted peanuts.
Eat immediately.
why_it_works: Kanda-lasun masala is normally reserved for curries; using it to season a simple curd bowl is a genuinely unusual, distinctive application specific to Kolhapur's spice tradition
Very low effort, entirely no-cook
Peanuts add protein and crunch

name: ZITLAS Puran Poli Ladoo-Style Bites
description: The traditional puran poli filling (jaggery-sweetened chana dal) rolled into small bite-sized balls instead of being encased in a rolled flatbread — a genuinely different construction from the Portion-Controlled Puran Poli already in the database.
ingredients: Chana dal, cooked and mashed — 100 g
instructions: Cook mashed chana dal with jaggery on low heat, stirring continuously, until it forms a very thick, dry paste (drier than for stuffing a poli).
Stir in cardamom powder.
Cool slightly and roll into 8 small balls.
Store in an airtight container for up to a week.
why_it_works: No flatbread wrapping at all — this is purely the traditional puran filling shaped into portable bites, a genuinely different format from the wrapped poli already in the database
Chana dal itself contributes real protein, unlike a purely sugar-based sweet
Portable, no cooking of a separate dough needed

name: ZITLAS Kolhapuri Misal Deluxe Bowl
description: A richer version of misal topped with a boiled egg and extra peanuts — a more indulgent 'special' variant distinct from the standard breakfast and lunchbox misal preparations already in the database.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft, add goda masala.
Add boiled matki with water and simmer 10 minutes into a gravy.
Top with a halved boiled egg and a scatter of extra peanuts just before serving.
Serve as a special, more filling version of misal.
why_it_works: The egg-and-extra-peanut topping makes this a deliberately richer, higher-protein 'special' version, genuinely different in composition and purpose from the everyday misal recipes already in the database
Highest protein of any misal-style dish in the database thanks to the combined legume-egg-peanut protein
Positioned as an occasional indulgence rather than an everyday meal

name: ZITLAS Shrikhand Protein Bowl
description: Hung curd whipped with cardamom and saffron, with a spoon of Greek yogurt blended in for extra protein — a lightened, protein-boosted take on the classic Maharashtrian festive dessert.
instructions: Hang curd in a muslin cloth for several hours to drain excess whey, leaving a thick base (chakka).
Whisk the hung curd with Greek yogurt, sugar or jaggery, cardamom powder and a few saffron strands until smooth.
Chill for at least 30 minutes before serving.
Note: hanging time folded into prep above.
why_it_works: Blending in Greek yogurt raises the protein meaningfully above a traditional shrikhand
Portion-controlled dessert bowl rather than a large festive serving
Classic Maharashtrian sweet made into a more considered everyday treat

name: ZITLAS Basundi Protein Bowl
description: A reduced, sweetened milk dessert finished with a spoon of milk powder for extra protein and nuts for texture — a portion-controlled version of the rich Maharashtrian classic.
instructions: Simmer milk on low heat, stirring occasionally, until it reduces by roughly half, about 18-20 minutes.
Stir in milk powder, jaggery and cardamom powder.
Top with crushed almonds and serve warm or chilled in a small bowl.
why_it_works: Milk powder addition raises the protein notably above a traditional basundi
Single, portion-controlled serving rather than a large festive batch
Almonds add healthy fat and crunch

name: ZITLAS Ukadiche Modak Bites
description: Traditional steamed rice-flour dumplings filled with sweet coconut and jaggery, made in a smaller, portion-controlled batch — the sweet counterpart to the savoury modak-inspired recipes already in the database.
instructions: Knead rice flour with boiling water into a smooth, pliable dough.
Cook grated coconut with jaggery and cardamom powder in a pan until it thickens into a sweet filling.
Shape small discs of dough, pleat the edges, fill with the coconut-jaggery mixture, and gather into the traditional modak shape.
Steam in a pressure cooker (without the whistle) for 12-15 minutes.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: The authentic sweet festive version, distinct from the savoury moong- and soya-filled modak adaptations already in the database
Smaller batch and portion size than a festival-scale preparation
Traditional shape and technique preserved, genuinely representing Maharashtra's most iconic sweet

name: ZITLAS Sabudana Kheer Protein Bowl
description: A milk-based sabudana kheer finished with a little milk powder for extra protein — a dessert use of sabudana, distinct from its khichdi, vada, thalipeeth, khichu and idli-style forms already in the database.
instructions: Simmer soaked sabudana in milk for 12-15 minutes until translucent and the milk thickens.
Stir in milk powder, jaggery and cardamom powder.
Serve warm or chilled.
why_it_works: Dessert kheer format is the sixth genuinely distinct use of sabudana across the database, alongside khichdi, vada, thalipeeth, khichu and idli-style steaming
Milk powder gives more protein than a traditional kheer
Comforting, familiar sweet

name: ZITLAS Modak Protein Bites
description: No-cook bites shaped like modak, made from crushed makhana, coconut and dates bound together — a raw, unsteamed dessert alternative to the traditional steamed modak already in this collection.
instructions: Blend dates into a sticky paste.
Mix in crushed makhana and grated coconut until well combined into a firm, moist mixture.
Shape by hand into a rough modak-like point at the top (or simply round balls if a mould isn't available).
Chill for 20 minutes before serving; store refrigerated for up to a week.
why_it_works: Entirely no-cook, unlike the steamed Ukadiche Modak Bites in this collection, offering a genuinely different preparation method for users without steaming equipment
Makhana and coconut give a distinct texture from a typical date-nut energy bite
Shape nods to the traditional festive sweet while being a fundamentally different recipe

name: ZITLAS Chilled Solkadhi Drink
description: A pure, chilled kokum-and-coconut-milk drink served on its own — a standalone beverage distinct from the breakfast Solkadhi-and-chana or dinner Solkadhi-and-rice combos already in the database.
instructions: Soak kokum in a little warm water to extract its colour and tang.
Whisk the kokum water into coconut milk with garlic, cumin and green chilli, thinning with plain water.
Chill and serve as a standalone cooling drink.
why_it_works: Served purely as a drink, without a food pairing, distinct from the breakfast and dinner combo uses of solkadhi already in the database
Deeply cooling, traditionally drunk on its own after a heavy or spicy meal
Very low calorie

name: ZITLAS Kokum Sherbet Protein Drink
description: A sweet-tart kokum sherbet blended with a spoon of Greek yogurt for protein — a distinctly sweeter, dessert-drink use of kokum from the savoury solkadhi preparations already in the database.
ingredients: Kokum syrup or soaked kokum — 30 g
instructions: Blend soaked kokum (or kokum syrup) with Greek yogurt, water and sugar or jaggery until smooth.
Chill and serve over ice if available.
why_it_works: Sweet sherbet style is a genuinely different use of kokum from the savoury, garlic-cumin solkadhi drinks already in the database
Greek yogurt adds protein a traditional sherbet lacks entirely
Bright pink colour and tart-sweet flavour, distinctly different drink experience

name: ZITLAS Sol Kadhi Buttermilk Fusion
description: A hybrid drink combining kokum-coconut solkadhi with spiced buttermilk — a distinct fusion not resembling either the pure solkadhi or a plain chaas already in the database.
instructions: Soak kokum in warm water.
Whisk the kokum water with coconut milk and buttermilk, along with roasted cumin powder.
Chill and serve.
why_it_works: Combining two distinct Maharashtrian cooling drinks into one fusion gives a genuinely different flavour and protein profile from either alone
Buttermilk adds real protein missing from a pure solkadhi
Very refreshing, low calorie

name: ZITLAS Kairi Panha Cooler Drink
description: A diluted, drinkable raw mango cooler, distinct from the thick pulped Aamras or the panha-with-sattu combo already in the database by being served purely as a light, sippable drink.
ingredients: Raw mango, boiled and pulped — 60 g
Roasted cumin powder, black salt — 2 g
instructions: Boil the raw mango until soft, then pulp it.
Mix the pulp with jaggery, water, roasted cumin powder and black salt, diluting to a thin, drinkable consistency.
Chill and serve.
why_it_works: Served purely as a light sipping drink rather than paired with sattu for protein, this is a genuinely different, simpler use of panha from the earlier combo recipe
Very cooling, traditional Maharashtrian summer refreshment
Naturally low calorie

name: ZITLAS Curd Chaas Jeera Drink
description: A simple spiced buttermilk with roasted cumin and curry leaves — a plain, everyday Maharashtrian chaas distinct from the fusion or fruit-based drinks already in this collection.
ingredients: Roasted cumin powder, curry leaves, black salt — 3 g
instructions: Whisk curd with water until smooth and frothy.
Stir in roasted cumin powder, finely chopped curry leaves and black salt.
Serve chilled.
why_it_works: The simplest, most everyday version of chaas in the collection, genuinely distinct from the kokum-fusion or fruit-based drinks by being unadorned and traditional
Very low cost, made from ingredients almost every household has
Classic digestive drink after a meal
